clue.text: Hear by means of vibration

indicators.note: hearing a word asks the solver to go by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: per is Latin-derived for by means of, as in 'per post'

explanation.surface: An instruction for perceiving sound through the body, as a deaf person might feel music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' looks like the definition, but it tells you to listen: PER said aloud matches PURR.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's contented rumbling is a low continuous throat sound, felt as much as heard.

clue.text: Ace coppers working for humanitarians

indicators.note: something working is being operated and set in motion, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Brilliant police officers doing volunteer work for aid organisations.
explanation.walkthrough: The PEACE CORPS is the American government volunteer programme that sends people to help developing countries.
explanation.definitionFit: Its volunteers carry out aid and development work abroad, a body of people devoted to human welfare.

clue.text: Engineers start to sand, fit last two components of mantle and rearrange cabinet

indicators.note: the start of the following word means only its opening letter is kept
only the final pair of letters of the following word is wanted

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
opening letter of sand
a fit of pique is a huff
the closing two letters of mantle

explanation.surface: Builders sanding, fitting a mantelpiece and moving the furniture around in a cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests a cupboard in the scene, but with 'rearrange' it is the government's ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime minister's reshuffle moves ministers between posts, changing the line-up of government.

clue.text: Cancer - not initially just a wild crab?

indicators.note: not the initial letter means the opening letter of the next word is dropped
wild letters are out of control and fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
just without its first letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the star sign Cancer nothing more than an untamed crab?
explanation.walkthrough: Cancer is the zodiac sign of the crab, which ties the surface together; the question mark flags that a crab is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs belong to the class of shelled arthropods along with lobsters and shrimps, so a crab is one example.

clue.text: Priest interrupts Roman Catholic memorial

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
Eli is the Old Testament priest who taught Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest breaking into a Catholic memorial service.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is the usual crossword priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something kept as a reminder of a person or past age, serving as a memento.

clue.text: Player in the middle of team, namely Fulham, runs all over the place

definitions.text: Player in the middle of team

indicators.note: scattered all over the place means the letters are strewn and gathered in a new order

blocks.note: sc. abbreviates scilicet, Latin for namely
taken as written
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A midfielder for Fulham, the London football club, charges about the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests football, but the definition is a rugby position; Fulham is just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby the scrum-half links forwards and backs, feeding the scrum from the centre of play.

clue.text: M C Escher's gutted after a news column regularly holds suspicion of copying

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter at even spacing
a mere suspicion is only a trace, so just the opening letter is used
a gutted fish has its insides removed, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its other form
N is a common abbreviation for new(s)
second, fourth and sixth letters of column
opening letter of copying
the first and last letters of Escher

explanation.surface: The Dutch artist M C Escher is devastated after a newspaper column hints he copied his work.
explanation.walkthrough: M C looks like the artist's initials, but it is the definition: master of ceremonies. Escher's pieces come last though printed first, as 'after' says.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies introduces acts and speakers at an event, presenting them to the audience.

clue.text: Times editor's beginning to strike

indicators.note: the beginning of the word means only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: eras are periods of history
opening letter of editor

explanation.surface: The editor of The Times newspaper is starting to take industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' reads as the newspaper, but it is simply a plural of time.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike out a word is to delete it, so strike can mean wipe away or remove.

clue.text: Snoopy's very big in New York

indicators.note: one element sits within the other one

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
OS is the clothing size outsize

explanation.surface: The cartoon beagle from Peanuts is a hit in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Snoopy looks like the dog's name, but here it is the adjective for someone who pries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone snoopy pokes into other people's business, which is exactly being inquisitive or prying.

clue.text: Order one to infiltrate right after onset of war

indicators.note: the onset is the very start, so just the opening letter is kept
infiltrating means getting inside, so one piece is placed within another
after places one piece following the other in reading order

blocks.note: opening letter of war
standard abbreviation
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An order sends a lone agent behind enemy lines as war breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: A court document commanding someone to act or refrain from acting is a formal legal command.

clue.text: Family-friendly parts of stars from the south

indicators.note: to part something is to split it open, so the first piece goes into the gap

blocks.note: U is the British film certificate for universal, suitable for all
astral means relating to the stars

explanation.surface: Child-friendly segments of celestial bodies seen from the southern hemisphere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun but is the verb: U splits ASTRAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Austral is a formal adjective for southern, as in Australia and the aurora australis.

clue.text: Car-free roads almost certainly carrying dull person back

indicators.note: almost all of the word means its final letter is cut
carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other
going back means reading the letters from right to left

blocks.note: sure is an emphatic yes, certainly
a yawn is a bore, a tedious person or thing

explanation.surface: Pedestrianised streets that will very likely bring a dreary person back.
explanation.walkthrough: SURE loses its E, then holds YAWN, and the whole is read in the opposite direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Airport strips are long paved tracks for aircraft, where no cars drive, so they are roads without cars.

clue.text: Dealer up town smuggles blow

indicators.note: smuggled goods are concealed inside, so the answer is tucked within the words

blocks.note: concealed across the end of dealer, all of up and the start of town

explanation.surface: A drug dealer in the posh part of town is sneaking in cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow' is slang for cocaine in the surface; as the definition it is a verb, to blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcano that blows its top bursts out violently, so blow means explode or burst forth.

clue.text: Got to work with limited time

blocks.note: first meaning: travelled to the office as a daily routine
second meaning: of a sentence, reduced to a shorter term

explanation.surface: Arrived at the office despite a tight schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is legal: a prisoner whose sentence is shortened has had it commuted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both making the daily journey to a job and having a punishment reduced to something lighter.

clue.text: Trees meant to be chopped up to reveal writing on road sign

indicators.note: chopping something up breaks it into pieces that can be put back in another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Roadside trees destined to be felled so that a road sign can be seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The words on a sign at a corner identify the road, giving its official title.

clue.text: Sea captain's log showing location of hidden treasure?

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: a record of events kept away from land
second meaning: a bank in a tax haven where wealth is stashed

explanation.surface: A pirate captain's journal reveals where the buried treasure is.
explanation.walkthrough: The pirate picture misleads: the treasure is money concealed from the taxman, and the log becomes an account kept at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bank holdings in a foreign tax haven are a classic way of keeping wealth concealed from authorities.

clue.text: Maybe Robbie's upset following his chart

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads upward
following places one piece after the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Margot Robbie is the Australian actress; maybe flags an example

explanation.surface: Perhaps Robbie Williams is cross after his place in the music charts.
explanation.walkthrough: Robbie suggests the pop singer and charts, but the Robbie needed is a surname: the actress Margot Robbie.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar diagram showing frequencies with columns is a kind of statistical graph.

clue.text: US President's grave about to be robbed by liberal, source claims

indicators.note: being robbed means something is taken and the thief takes its place here
to claim is to take hold of, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a root is an origin or source
grave and severe both mean serious
re means concerning, about
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A US President's tomb is going to be raided by a left-winger, according to a source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Robbed by liberal' means the about-word is stolen and L takes its place. 'Source claims' sounds like reported speech but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore and Franklin D. Roosevelt were both presidents of the United States.

clue.text: Strange peacekeepers catch the sun when travelling up river

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: United Nations peacekeeping forces
to tan is to get brown in the sun
the Ural is a river in Russia and Kazakhstan

explanation.surface: Odd that soldiers on peace missions sunbathe while moving upstream.
explanation.definitionFit: Something against nature is abnormal or odd, so the word fits peculiar or weird.

clue.text: Make pear juice for meeting?

blocks.note: surface reading: squeeze fruit to extract its juice
setter's reading: a Conference is a pear variety, so crushing one names a gathering with journalists

explanation.surface: Instructions for pressing pears to make a drink for a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is a common British pear variety, which is the pun the whole clue turns on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering at which officials answer questions from reporters is a media briefing.

clue.text: Penile fractures getting caught after old age

indicators.note: a fracture breaks something apart, so the letters are reassembled differently
after places one piece following another
getting something means taking it in, so a pair of letters goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation
C is cricket shorthand for caught

explanation.surface: An embarrassing injury becomes more common in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: C is placed after O to make OC, which goes inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pliocene is a geological epoch, a span of time roughly five to two and a half million years ago.

clue.text: Place for Don McLean's car - Cybertruck, perhaps - in shelter?

indicators.note: one piece sits within another

blocks.note: lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
the Tesla Cybertruck is an electric vehicle, EV; perhaps marks an example

explanation.surface: Wondering where the singer Don McLean might park a Tesla Cybertruck under cover.
explanation.walkthrough: In his song American Pie, Don McLean 'drove my Chevy to the levee'.
explanation.definitionFit: An embankment along a river is where the song's narrator drove his Chevrolet.

clue.text: Follow around, nearly unseen

indicators.note: nearly all of the word means its final letter is removed
letters moved around end up in a new order

blocks.note: unseen without its final letter

explanation.surface: Tail someone closely while staying almost invisible.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come afterwards as a result, the sense of follow in 'chaos followed'.

clue.text: Had sex, I understand

blocks.note: first meaning: a slang phrase for sleeping together
second meaning: an informal reply meaning the point is clear

explanation.walkthrough: The comma makes it read like a confession followed by a sympathetic reply; the two are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for physical intimacy and a casual way of saying a message has been grasped.

clue.text: Turn on live broadcast of desert

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places one piece above the next
something broadcast is heard over the air, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a go is a turn in a game
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Switch on a live TV programme about the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live broadcast' reads as a TV term, but the two words do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is the vast arid region spanning northern China and southern Mongolia.

clue.text: Pine hedged back by magnolia

indicators.note: hedged in means enclosed, so the letters are surrounded by the word
back means the letters are read in the other direction

blocks.note: the middle letters of magnolia

explanation.surface: A pine tree screened behind a magnolia in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a tree to match the magnolia, but it is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for someone is to yearn for them, the same as longing.

clue.text: Job I view is reserved in prime positions for heads

indicators.note: positions numbered by prime numbers, the second, third, fifth, seventh and so on, are the ones kept

blocks.note: letters 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13 and 17 of the phrase

explanation.surface: A jobseeker considers which posts are held back for heads of department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prime positions' sounds like top jobs, but it means the prime-numbered places in the letter string.
explanation.definitionFit: The face of a coin bearing the monarch's portrait is its main side, so heads names it.

clue.text: Cold region of southern Spain and Portugal

blocks.note: standard abbreviation
the Iberian peninsula holds both countries

explanation.surface: A chilly part of the Iberian peninsula's south.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a deliberate contradiction: southern Spain is hardly cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia is the vast Russian territory famous for its freezing winters.

clue.text: Senior has problem with intellect

blocks.note: older people are grey-haired
as in what is the matter

explanation.surface: An elderly person struggles with mental sharpness.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain tissue associated with thinking is used informally for brainpower or intelligence.

clue.text: Regret switching hands on golf stick

indicators.note: changing from one hand to the other swaps right for left
in an across clue, on means placed after the next piece

blocks.note: G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A golfer regrets changing grip on a club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' means R and L, right and left: the R becomes L. 'Golf stick' is a red herring for a club; stick is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue is an adhesive, and as a verb it means to fasten things together.
